\chapter{Interference, allocation policies and software adoption}
\label{v13:sw-networks}

The preceding relationship analysis showed why a policy may require joint
graph and action information. This chapter examines the allocation problem
itself. It distinguishes network and grouped targets, develops the two initial
software references, and compares spatial, experimental, learned-policy and
simulation alternatives. The recurring small graphs and cost denominators are
matched comparison devices; each implementation's different assumptions and
failure conditions remain part of the argument.

\section{The unit receiving treatment need not be the independent unit}

A household member's offer can influence another member's borrowing, and an
outreach campaign can affect connected firms. In such settings a potential
outcome depends on more than the individual's own action. Writing only
$Y_i(a_i)$ hides the policy being evaluated. A more explicit representation is
$Y_i(a_i,\mathbf a_{-i})$, often restricted through an exposure mapping of
other units' actions. The mapping and the network are scientific inputs;
neither is established merely by finding matching customer identifiers.

Two broad software constructions appear in the inspected sources. MossSpider
uses a network and exposure summaries in a network-targeted estimation
workflow. Inferference uses grouped formulas, allocation probabilities and
inverse-probability weighting. These constructions have different observation
laws and potentially different targets. Their package names do not establish
interchangeability.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider,v13_sw_inferference}

An allocation policy illustrates the target. Suppose two linked borrowers have
binary outreach actions $A_1,A_2$, independently assigned with probability $p$
under the proposed policy. Stipulate the synthetic financial outcome
\[
 Y_i(a_i,a_j)=100a_i+40a_j-30a_i a_j
\]
in CNY. The first term represents the own-action contribution, the second a
spillover and the last diminishing combined benefit. These are hypothetical
structural values, not bank estimates. Averaging under the allocation gives
\[
 V(p)=140p-30p^2.
\]
For $p=0.2$ the mean is 26.8 CNY; for $p=0.8$ it is 92.8 CNY. The allocation
contrast is 66 CNY per borrower. Exact enumeration of the four assignments
checks the formula.\cite{v13_project_exact}

The direct effect of changing only the individual's own action is instead
$100-30a_j$, or $100-30p$ when the neighbor is independently treated with
probability $p$. This differs from the total allocation contrast. Reporting
one as the other can misprice the campaign even when every arithmetic
calculation is correct. The bank must specify whether it changes one action,
the neighborhood's allocation or an entire branch policy, and which costs
are included in the outcome.

\section{MossSpider: network semantics are part of the estimand}

The inspected \texttt{NetworkTMLE} documentation describes expected incidence
under a treatment plan, with Monte Carlo integration over allocations for
stochastic plans. It states a direct-contact interference assumption. The
constructor rejects self-loops, noninteger node identities and nonbinary
exposure, creates a relabeled network while retaining original identities,
and constructs an unweighted adjacency matrix.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider}

These details matter for bank graphs. A weighted guarantee network is not the
same as an unweighted adjacency graph. Removing weights can turn a small
guarantee into the same exposure contribution as a large one. Relabeling nodes
is harmless only when results can be mapped back to the correct identities.
A linkage error can attach the correct numerical estimate to the wrong firm.
Semantic conformance therefore needs an identity roundtrip and an explicit
policy for unsupported weighted relationships.

Direction requires particular review. The documentation initially describes an
undirected graph but also explains a directed influence convention opposite
the graph arrow, and the selected constructor includes directed handling. This
combination requires a concrete test with an asymmetric small graph. One should
not infer direction from a diagram's appearance or assume that every library
uses source-to-target influence. A two-node one-way example with distinguishable
covariates can determine which neighbor contributes to each exposure summary.
Section~\ref{sec:exec24-interference-reuse} develops the selected mapping,
policy and variance paths. Their inspected direction convention still needs
matched native tests; directed bank-network adoption remains a proposed use.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider}

Degree restrictions also change the target. The documentation treats nodes
outside a requested degree range as background, with their exposures unchanged
by the intervention. This can be scientifically useful, but it is not the
same as deleting those nodes from the graph or intervening on all customers.
The response must state which nodes are in the target population, which remain
background and how their factual exposure affects the intervention outcome.

The source disclaims a missing-data procedure. Missing node attributes,
uncertain links and omitted customers are common in banking, but the existence
of an exposure-mapping function does not solve those observation problems.
One must either supply defensible complete data in the declared regime or
develop a separate missingness/linkage construction. Network-targeted estimation
does not automatically qualify ownership or inclusion truth.

The observed MIT text makes a restricted adapter worth considering. Full adoption
requires qualification of the exposure-model and mapping code, targeting step,
Monte Carlo integration and variance calculation, together with actual
dependency/runtime checks. The developed study retains deterministic-policy
refusals, background-node treatment and a potentially negative variance
quadratic; these restrictions belong in any proposed adapter. A claim of general contagion, dynamic financial-network equilibrium or
arbitrary spillovers would go beyond the selected implementation evidence.

\section{Inferference: grouped allocation and numerical integration}

The inspected \texttt{interference} function uses a formula that identifies
outcome, exposure, optional participation, propensity covariates and a grouping
variable. It accepts allocation probabilities and propensity-model choices
including \texttt{glm}, \texttt{glmer}, \texttt{HLfit} and an oracle route.
Its documented causal-estimation path is IPW with naive or robust variance
options. The selected code sorts records by group and checks group count,
allocation range and the variance option.\cite{v13_sw_inferference}

A group-based model can be appropriate when the scientific design justifies
within-group interference and the required between-group sampling assumptions.
It does not become a model of arbitrary connected borrowers by assigning
everyone a group label. Cross-group guarantees or shared market shocks can
violate the intended observation law. The grouping decision needs domain
evidence and should be subjected to sensitivity analysis where boundaries
are uncertain.

The default logit integrand is restricted to a single random effect in the
documented implementation. The code rejects more than one when that integrand
is selected. Thus a proposal with household and branch random effects needs a
different justified integration path; silently dropping one random effect is
a model change. An oracle propensity option is useful for synthetic reference
calculations, but supplied true parameters cannot be counted as evidence that
an estimated-propensity workflow is calibrated.

There is also a reproducibility issue visible directly in the source. The prose
describes \texttt{integrate\_allocation} as defaulting to false, while the
inspected function signature sets it to true. The proper response is to specify
and record the argument explicitly. Section~\ref{sec:exec24-interference-reuse}
traces the downstream ratio and derivative paths; their flag propagation,
allocation-mass and missing-group restrictions still require matched native
qualification. It is not appropriate to select whichever default gives a more
favorable result after comparing outputs.\cite{v13_sw_inferference}

For large groups, multiplying many probabilities can create numerical problems.
The documentation discusses an allocation-integration option in this context.
Qualification should include large and uneven groups, boundary allocation
probabilities, integration tolerances and variance derivatives. A successful
floating-point result does not prove adequate support; an underflow error does
not prove nonidentification. These are different failure modes and need
different diagnostics.

The observed DESCRIPTION declares GPL version 2 or later and a dated version.
That informs a dependency review but does not establish the license status of
every linked component or distribution arrangement. A candidate grouped-policy
reference should remain distinct from a decision to embed or port it.

\section{A common comparison must distinguish network and group assumptions}

The two packages can be compared on a common small allocation problem only
after their target, exposure mapping and sampling assumptions are aligned.
For the two-borrower example, the exact four-assignment enumeration supplies a
transparent functional reference. A larger benchmark should vary degree,
group size, allocation probability, support, observation errors and dependence.
It should include examples where a direct-contact or group restriction is false.

Metrics should separate the target mean, direct and spillover contrasts,
coverage, finite availability, Monte Carlo integration error and total cost.
Increasing simulated allocations reduces integration error conditional on a
fitted model. It does not create independent groups or validate the graph.
Uncertainty must follow the actual sampling unit; counting nodes as independent
merely because the graph is stored in a table can produce misleading precision.

The implementation contract should retain the original graph, its direction
and weights, the identity map, intervention population, allocation rule,
background nodes and exposure mapping. A result should be rejected as
semantically incompatible if a proposed bridge silently changes any of these.
This requirement is shared by library calls, command-line jobs and agent tools.
An interface can make a scientific restriction visible; it cannot make it true.

\section{Provisional reuse choices and the evidence needed to change them}

The inspected software supports a portfolio of candidate components rather
than a single universal engine. The following choices describe potential uses and qualification conditions,
not accepted integrations or benchmarks. The earlier functional and
longitudinal chapters develop the corresponding source findings
(Chapters~\ref{v13:sw-functional} and~\ref{v13:sw-regimes}); the table retains
the conditions that must survive implementation rather than treating those
studies as still absent.

\begin{longtable}{p{0.18\textwidth}p{0.34\textwidth}p{0.39\textwidth}}
\toprule
Component & Candidate role & Conditions to preserve and qualify\\
\midrule
\endhead
DirectLiNGAM & Functional discovery adapter & Reviewed base-class behavior, prior orientation,
functional assumptions and adverse latent/Gaussian cases\\
y0 & Symbolic ID/IDC adapter & Reviewed recursive paths, conditional-path restriction,
graph validation, expression roundtrip and nonidentification references\\
delicatessen & Equation and numerical reference & Solver, Jacobian, covariance,
sampling unit and complete dependency contract\\
statsmodels & Point-treatment GMM baseline & Matched population, propensity bounds,
actual covariance behavior and dependent-data limits\\
pygformula & Longitudinal-regime adapter & History/event meaning, simulation,
bootstrap unit, diagnostics and policy scope\\
grf & R/native heterogeneous-effect component & Native algorithms, variance,
aggregation measure, ABI and license/distribution review\\
CausalGPS & Continuous-density component & Density/transformation helpers,
counterfactual doses, support and downstream estimation\\
causaldrf & Dose-response reference & Full function, interval procedures,
support, recovered holder notice and dependency terms\\
MossSpider & Restricted network-policy component & Direction, mapping, identity,
targeting, variance and observation restrictions\\
inferference & Grouped-allocation reference & Integrands, numerical defaults,
variance, group law and dependency terms\\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

An integration decision is stronger than identifying a promising function.
Direct adoption needs a stable, compatible dependency and scientific contract.
An adapter needs semantic parity and error preservation. A port needs the right
to reuse the implementation, an upstream behavioral oracle, independent
references, numerical/statistical equivalence criteria and a maintenance owner.
A research reference can be valuable without becoming a product dependency.
Deferral is justified when these prerequisites are missing; rejection should
state a concrete incompatibility and a revisit condition.

Commercial comparison must apply the same discipline. Vendor documentation can
establish a dated documented feature, but not measured agreement or operating
cost without an executed comparison. An inaccessible manual cannot support a
claim that the vendor lacks an operation. Our proposed graph-to-effect or
banking workflow is likewise not a delivered competitive advantage. A sound
build/buy/partner decision compares the vendor's documented and measured state
with our implemented, conditional, proposed or absent state, and makes the
missing evidence explicit.

Licensing is one part of this decision. The selected MIT and BSD texts,
repository GPL text and package license declarations provide traceable starting
points. Dependencies, bundled data, separate notices, native libraries and the
intended distribution arrangement still need review. A subprocess boundary
does not automatically settle licensing obligations, just as a Python wrapper
does not establish that a native operation has been qualified.

The software survey can therefore guide implementation immediately without
claiming premature adoption. It identifies precise operations, preserves their
mathematical meaning and specifies the evidence needed for the next decision.
Runtime, bank validation and independent scientific acceptance remain separate
from these source-grounded provisional choices.

deterministic validator checks the declared operation against its supported
combinations. An LLM's plausible description is not evidence that a package
uses the intended covariance or intervention target.

the same estimand and information across packages, separates sampling from

\chapter{What language models contribute to causal knowledge}
\label{la:frontier}

Section~\ref{scisyn:assistance} gives the principal recommendation for language
assistance. This chapter develops its evidential basis. It first distinguishes
knowledge, formal reasoning, mechanism proposals and workflow support, then
asks how published evaluations transfer to a banking decision. Exact examples
show how task mixtures, shared errors and unresolved causal models can change
that decision. The final comparisons examine consistency judges, orchestration,
literature extraction and the design of a versioned assistance experiment.

\section{Four different questions about cause and effect}

A banker asking why deposit balances fell can be asking for an explanation of
a recorded event, an estimate of a feasible rate intervention, a prediction of
next month's balance, or a diagnosis of an observation error. A fluent answer
can move between these objects without announcing the change. Evaluating assistance therefore starts by distinguishing the task: a proposed scientific question, evidence about a causal model,
a formal calculation conditional on that model, or a recommendation under a
specified loss. Success on one task does not establish success on the others.

The early frontier argument proposes using language models to organize domain
knowledge, draft graphs, critique assumptions and suggest robustness analyses.
It also records the ability to reproduce recognizable public data and
distinguishes transforming known information from discovering a new causal
structure.\cite{v12_la_2305_00050} This distinction is particularly consequential
in banking. A familiar statement about interest rates can be useful prior
knowledge, but the effect of a particular bank's deposit offer depends on its
population, competitors, eligibility rules and information clock. A remembered
relationship does not determine that intervention effect.

Formal benchmarks introduce a second object. CLadder constructs questions from
known causal structures with different verbalizations. Its results concern
answers to those generated questions, including historically specified models
and prompting methods.\cite{v12_la_2312_04350} Such a benchmark can reveal failures
to distinguish observation from intervention. It cannot establish that a model
elicits the right variables from an unfamiliar bank process, measures them
correctly, or returns calibrated uncertainty after fitting to dependent data.
These are additional stages of the proposed product.

\chapter{Translating a banking decision into a causal question}
\label{la:translation}

The preceding evidence review leaves a practical starting point: assistance
must preserve the question before it can improve an answer. This chapter
builds that question from population, action, outcome, loss and information
time. Incentive and servicing examples expose common substitutions; a
literature-graph study separates extracted claims from hypotheses; the
formulation workflow then leads to robust population comparisons and goal
clarification. Together these treatments explain which commitments an analyst
must resolve and which alternatives an assistant must retain.

\section{A business sentence can contain several questions}

``Should we increase the deposit offer?'' sounds like a single question, but
it leaves several choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change
in the quoted rate, the eligibility rule, the message shown to a customer or
the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The outcome could be a new
deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value. The
population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or
everyone eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different
causal problem.

A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence
needed to resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate
and silently treat that target as the owner's decision. In the project funding
case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point increase and the change in
net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates. Their
business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are
not identical. The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure
that must be hidden by returning a number.

The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression
from a scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and
interpretation. Their illustrative medical examples attend to eligibility,
baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected paper also reports that
generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying those
principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not
validate banking clocks or interventions.\cite{v12_la_2407_19118}

\section{A question as a collection of commitments}

The project represents a question as
\begin{equation}
 Q=(\mathcal U,P,\mathcal A,\pi,\pi_0,Y,H,\nu,\ell,\mathcal I).
 \label{la:question}
\end{equation}
Here \(\mathcal U\) is the unit of analysis; \(P\) is the target population;
\(\mathcal A\) is the feasible action set; \(\pi\) and \(\pi_0\) are the
policy and comparator; \(Y\) is the outcome; \(H\) is the horizon; \(\nu\)
is the measure used to average over the population; \(\ell\) is the loss,
including its units; and \(\mathcal I\) specifies information available at
each action. This notation defines the project's declaration contract. It is
not an identification theorem.

The unit needs particular care. An account can be an observation while a
customer is the decision unit and a household is the unit within which actions
interact. An assistant can ask which role each identifier plays, but a column
called customer ID does not certify ownership or stable linkage. If several
accounts share a budget or pricing rule, an account-level action may also be
an infeasible description of the intervention. The feasible action set should
reflect what the responsible institution can actually change.

The comparator must be as explicit as the intervention. ``No treatment'' might
mean no new contact, continuation of the current contact policy, no rate
increase, or a different offer under a fixed budget. A dynamic policy can
include future actions conditional on history, so its comparator is also a
history-dependent rule. An effect relative to one comparator cannot be
reused for another solely because the same treatment variable appears in the
dataset.

The outcome and loss should also remain separate. A change in balances has
units of currency held over a horizon; funding expense combines balances,
rates and time. A larger deposit balance can have a positive acquisition
interpretation and an unfavorable net-cost implication. If \(g(a)\) is a
specified gross benefit and \(c(a)\) is a specified cost, the decision may
depend on \(E[g(a)-c(a)]\), not on \(E[g(a)]\) alone. The definitions and
valuation assumptions must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful.
The assistant should make missing costs visible rather than invent prices.

\section{Changing a population measure changes the answer}

Let \(X\) denote baseline features and let
\(\tau(x)=E[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x]\). A weighted target can be written
\begin{equation}
 \theta_w=\frac{E[w(X)\tau(X)]}{E[w(X)]},\qquad E[w(X)]>0.
 \label{la:weighted-target}
\end{equation}
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different
weights. Under the conditions that make a propensity \(e(x)=\Pr(A=1\mid X=x)\)
appropriate for the intended population, familiar choices are \(1\),
\(e(x)\), \(e(x)(1-e(x))\) and
\(1\{a\leq e(x)\leq b\}\), respectively. The formula records which average
is wanted. It does not establish exchangeability, support, estimation rates
or coverage.

An exact project example makes the distinction visible. Let two strata have
equal population probability, with propensities \(0.2\) and \(0.5\), and
effects \(0\) and \(10\). Trimming to \([0.1,0.9]\) keeps both strata, so
the trimmed-population effect is \(5\). Overlap weights are \(0.16\) and
\(0.25\), giving
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{overlap}}=
 \frac{0.16(0)+0.25(10)}{0.16+0.25}=\frac{250}{41}
 =6.09756\ldots.
\]
Both calculations can be exact and still answer different questions. A label
such as ``overlap population'' is insufficient if its underlying weighting
rule is not retained.

This issue is directly relevant to the inspected OCI agent paper. Chou and
colleagues describe a principal/actor/critic workflow, reproducible notebooks,
point-in-time estimation and overlap diagnostics. The inspected trimming
passage uses a target label that must be reconciled with the actual weighting
rule before mapping it to conventional overlap weighting. The proposed
architecture is informative, but an assistant should not inherit a target
label without checking its definition.\cite{v12_la_2607_22443}

Changing the target to remove unsupported accounts can be scientifically
reasonable, but it is a new decision question. A bank owner may care about
precisely those accounts for which treatment support is weak. An honest report
can say that a narrower target is estimable under the supplied assumptions
while the original target remains unresolved. It should show the excluded
population, the new averaging rule and the implications for the decision.

\section{Information is governed by an availability clock}

The date on which an event occurred differs from the date on which an analyst
or policy could observe it. For a recorded variable \(V\), write \(e_V\) for
event time and \(a_V\) for availability time. The finite project fixtures
require \(e_V\leq a_V\), and a policy acting at time \(t\) can use the value
only if \(a_V\leq t\). A derived feature becomes available no earlier than
its required inputs. These rules prevent an apparently historical feature
from leaking future information into a decision.

In the servicing fixture, an account condition occurs at day ten but becomes
available at day eleven. A rule acting on day eleven may use it; a rule acting
on day ten may not. The distinction matters even when both values later appear
in the same warehouse table. A language assistant should request the recording
and availability convention, rather than infer it from a field name or a
sorted timestamp.

Advance announcements and forecasts require different variable definitions.
A forecast observed today of next month's condition is a current forecast
variable, not a measurement of a future realized condition with an impossible
availability time. Revised historical data similarly require a vintage or
revision convention. The project's finite validator does not implement every
revision protocol. It checks the stated recorded-value contract and leaves
more complex clocks as explicit extensions.

Equal timestamps do not determine direction. Two columns aggregated to the
same day may hide a finer action sequence or a common cause. The assistant
can propose a finer clock and identify the evidence needed to support it.
It cannot establish temporal precedence by placing one variable first in a
diagram. When the granularity is insufficient, the ambiguity should survive
into the model class.

\section{An available covariate is not automatically an adjustment variable}

In a sequential servicing model, \(A_0\) changes an intermediate condition
\(L_1\), which affects both a later action \(A_1\) and the outcome \(Y\).
The same \(L_1\) is a mediator for the first action and a common cause of the
second action--outcome relation. Its appropriate use depends on the target.
Including every available column in one regression does not preserve all
possible total, direct and policy effects.

The project declaration therefore distinguishes a policy-history purpose
from an ordinary adjustment purpose. A simple directed-path diagnostic flags
a post-treatment descendant proposed as an ordinary total-effect control.
It does not declare all post-treatment conditioning invalid. Controlled
direct effects and longitudinal procedures need their own question and
formal analysis. A warning from a declaration validator is not a replacement
for an adjustment criterion or an identification algorithm.

Observation processes can alter the target in a similar way. Suppose only
successfully linked records enter an analysis and both action and repayment
affect successful linkage. The selection indicator is part of the causal
problem, and an effect among linked records may differ from an effect in the
original population. A record-link score is an observed proxy; it is not
verified ownership. The observation fixture deliberately retains a latent
ownership variable, a selection node and an unresolved population choice.

CausalDS provides a useful literature distinction here: its conceptual SCM
variables and its separate observation model are not interchangeable. The
paper's narrated synthetic scenes can test how an agent handles that
distinction, but they do not supply authentic banking semantic or assignment
truth.\cite{v12_la_2607_08093}

\section{The handoff to formal analysis}

The assistant's useful output is a reviewable declaration and a record of

\label{la:translation}

The preceding evidence review leaves a practical starting point: assistance
must preserve the question before it can improve an answer. This chapter
builds that question from population, action, outcome, loss and information

literature-graph study separates extracted claims from hypotheses; the
formulation workflow then leads to robust population comparisons and goal
clarification. Together these treatments explain which commitments an analyst
must resolve and which alternatives an assistant must retain.

\section{A business sentence can contain several questions}

``Should we increase the deposit offer?'' sounds like a single question, but
it leaves several choices unresolved. The intended action could be a change
in the quoted rate, the eligibility rule, the message shown to a customer or
the allocation of a fixed promotional budget. The outcome could be a new
deposit, retained balances, funding cost or total relationship value. The
population could be existing customers, applicants who received an offer or
everyone eligible under a proposed rule. Each choice defines a different
causal problem.

A language assistant can expose these alternatives and organize the evidence
needed to resolve them. It should not choose the easiest target to estimate
and silently treat that target as the owner's decision. In the project funding
case, the response of balances to a 25-basis-point increase and the change in
net funding cost over thirty days are retained as separate candidates. Their
business motivation is shared; their outcomes and decision consequences are
not identical. The unresolved choice is useful information, not a failure
that must be hidden by returning a number.

The co-pilot roadmap discussed by Alaa and colleagues motivates this progression
from a scientific question through assumptions, statistical targets and
interpretation. Their illustrative medical examples attend to eligibility,
baseline time, treatment and follow-up. The inspected paper also reports that
generic uncued answers can omit relevant design concerns. Applying those
principles to banking is a project proposal; the medical examples do not
validate banking clocks or interventions. \cite{v12_la_2407_19118}

The project represents a question as
\begin{equation}

 \label{la:question}
\end{equation}

not an identification theorem.

depend on \(E[g(a)-c(a)]\), not on \(E[g(a)]\) alone. The definitions and
valuation assumptions must be supplied before that subtraction is meaningful.

 \label{la:weighted-target}
\end{equation}
Uniform, treated-population, overlap and trimmed targets use different

or coverage.

\section{A complete translation example: the incentive question}
\label{v13:la-dose}

Suppose a manager asks an agent to ``find the incentive uplift and choose the
best offer.'' The sentence leaves at least three mathematical objects open:
a binary offer effect, a continuous local slope, and a finite-dose policy value.
The agent can help by presenting these alternatives with their populations,
units and action constraints. It should not select whichever object happens
to be exposed by the first available package.

Let $A$ be incentive intensity in a declared unit and let $Y$ be retained net
value over a fixed horizon. The finite question is
$\Delta(a_1,a_0)=\mathbb E\{Y(a_1)-Y(a_0)\}$. A local derivative, where it
exists, is $\mu'(a)$. A covariance slope averages features of the response
under an exposure distribution and need not equal either object. The inspected
grf and dose-response interfaces make this a practical interoperability issue,
not merely a linguistic distinction.\cite{v13_sw_grf,v13_sw_causaldrf}

For the stipulated curve $\mu(a)=20a-3a^2$, a uniform exposure on $[0,2]$
gives covariance slope 14, while moving from dose one to dose two changes the
mean by 11 CNY. An agent that labels 14 as the value of the specified change
has mistranslated the problem even if it calls its numerical tool correctly.
The exact project calculation makes the error detectable without a live model
experiment.\cite{v13_project_exact}

A useful translation record would therefore state: eligible existing customers;
the information available before the offer; current dose one and feasible dose
two; a fixed retention horizon; treatment and outcome currency units; and
whether incentive expense is already included in $Y$. If expense is excluded,
the decision value is $\Delta(a_1,a_0)-\{c(a_1)-c(a_0)\}$. Subtracting it again
when $Y$ already measures net value would double-count cost. The record also
needs account closure/default definitions and a sampling unit for uncertainty.

The agent's role can be useful at each handoff. It can flag unspecified units,
find source definitions, propose alternative causal questions and generate
typed requests. Formal checks can verify that a numerical result matches the
declared query. Domain owners must still confirm the feasible intervention and
measurement meanings; neither fluent prose nor a schema establishes them.

\section{A servicing policy is a rule with an information boundary}

For sequential servicing, an action rule uses $H_t$, the information actually
available at decision time. A data field recorded later may describe an earlier
event while remaining unavailable to the operating policy. An agent assembling
history features must preserve both event and availability times. Otherwise
the proposed policy uses information the bank would not possess when acting.

The causal query should distinguish evaluating a specified rule, choosing among
rules and claiming an optimal hidden-state policy. A longitudinal simulator can
evaluate supplied regimes under its assumptions. Its ability to accept a custom
history function does not identify private customer states or make an unknown
logger known. The inspected pygformula class exposes useful histories, event
and regime options, but its source interface alone establishes neither policy
optimality nor uncertainty under arbitrary dependence.\cite{v13_sw_pygformula}

A concrete policy-selection hazard can be shown without an asymptotic argument.
Suppose two equally valuable policies each have independent evaluation error
equal to minus one or plus one with equal probability. The maximum of the two
errors is minus one only when both are minus one, and plus one otherwise.
Its expectation is therefore $\tfrac34-\tfrac14=\tfrac12$. Reporting the
selected policy's same-data evaluation is optimistic. If the selected policy
is evaluated with a fresh independent error of mean zero, the evaluation error
has mean zero conditional on the selection. Exact enumeration verifies both
claims.\cite{v13_project_exact}

This example does not prove that a particular split is sufficient for a
dependent servicing panel. It explains why the selection and evaluation laws
must be specified. An agent can preserve the split, freeze candidate rules and
refuse reuse of a held-out set for tuning. A scientific argument must still
justify independence or the required dependence control. Training a policy
and then narrating its favorable development score is not an independent
evaluation.

\section{Translation outputs that deserve abstention}

Some business questions should produce a request for more information or a set
of alternatives. If ``the customer'' may mean the legal entity, the beneficial
owner or a linked household, choosing one silently changes both the population
and interference structure. If the intended action is not operationally
feasible, the mathematically optimal action is irrelevant. If the loss function
and costs are unknown, the agent can compare statistical targets but cannot
assert an investment recommendation.

Abstention should be specific. It should identify the missing definition,
record the alternative interpretations and explain which downstream operation
depends on the answer. That is different from a generic refusal to analyze.
For an incentive query, the missing item may be treatment units or whether
cost is already included. For servicing it may be the information clock or
the policy class. For interference it may be network direction or the allocation
policy. These are concrete commitments that owners can resolve and numerical
tools can then preserve.

\chapter{Variables, diagrams and justified disagreement}
\label{la:diagrams}

The preceding chapter established what definitions and fallible evidence can
contribute. Here those objects enter a reviewable diagram. The argument first
separates graph classes, premises and retrieval outcomes, then develops exact
proxy, collider, clock and disagreement examples. The ontology comparison
connects the diagram to implementable treatment versions and source records.
The final restrictions study follows a premise through both graph and effect
sets, showing why a smaller graph class need not settle the decision.

\section{From vocabulary to measured variables}

A useful causal diagram begins with variables whose meanings can survive
contact with data. A business glossary may contain ``risk,'' ``relationship''
and ``engagement,'' while a dataset contains a risk-score vintage, a set of
linked accounts and an observed click. Those are related concepts, but they
are not interchangeable causal variables. An assistant can propose mappings,
detect inconsistent names and assemble definitions. Each proposed mapping
still needs an operational meaning, a unit and an information clock.

OntoLearner offers relevant modular ideas for ontology loading, typing,
taxonomy and relation-learning tasks. The inspected paper reports
domain-dependent errors and retrieval failures. Its relation-learning
capability is not a guarantee that a relation is causal, or that a concept
has a valid measured proxy in the bank. Ontology alignment should therefore
precede and inform graph construction without being silently promoted into
causal identification.\cite{v12_la_2607_01977}

For example, ``customer owns account'' may describe a legal relation,
``records share an identifier'' an administrative relation, and ``records
have a high linkage score'' a model output. If ownership affects both offer
eligibility and repayment behavior, substituting the linkage score for
ownership leaves a measurement problem. Adding an arrow from the score to
repayment does not resolve it. The diagram should distinguish latent
ownership, observed records, the linkage procedure and sample selection.

Likewise, an ordinal description such as ``high influence'' cannot be used
as an effect size without a scale. An assistant's rating of a proposed edge
may express a preference among textual explanations. It is not automatically
a probability that the edge is present, a posterior over graphs, or a
confidence level. A typed diagram can retain such a rating as explicitly
uncalibrated metadata while refusing to use it as scientific evidence.

\section{What an edge asserts}

An edge proposal should state more than two variable names. The endpoint
marks identify the proposed graphical object. A source and inspected anchor
state what supports the proposal. A scope describes the population, period
and intervention to which that evidence applies. A counterevidence record
states whether contrary evidence was found, absent in the inspected material,
or not successfully searched. A review disposition records acceptance as a
premise, rejection, or unresolved status.

These fields serve different purposes. A source can be authentic but
inapplicable to the current banking action. A study can concern a different
population or a different definition of treatment. A plausible timing argument
can constrain direction without establishing that any causal connection
exists. The assistant should make the supported proposition as narrow as
the evidence warrants and retain the reasons for disagreement.

CausalChat supplies an example of interactive model development: the inspected
paper combines optional CPDAG discovery, model suggestions, graph editing
and structural-equation coefficient updates. Its prompts use ordinal
causal-significance ratings and ask for possible confounders and mediators.
These are useful interaction ideas. The paper's expert feedback also raises
missing citations and uncertainty about the quality of scientific evidence
provided by the model. A coefficient update after adding an edge cannot
establish that the edge itself is true.\cite{v12_la_2410_14146}

The proposed banking workflow retains the interaction but changes the
scientific handoff. An accepted premise is labeled as a premise with a
responsible review, not as a truth certified by the model. A model proposal
alone cannot remove an observationally compatible graph alternative. The
tool responsible for formal identification receives the complete reviewed
graph object and its restrictions, rather than a picture whose uncertainty
has disappeared in editing.

\section{Graph classes and collections of candidate models}

A CPDAG or PAG is a structured representation with its own interpretation.
A list of proposed DAGs is another object. A collection of edges marked
``possible'' is not automatically an enumeration of every combination of
those edges. Confusing these representations can silently exclude models
or include incompatible ones.

The project contract preserves a CPDAG or PAG directly when that is the
appropriate object, including circle endpoints. It also permits explicitly
listed candidate models. An edge marked possible within a candidate describes
the evidence status of that candidate's edge; it does not make all optional
edge combinations an exhaustive graph class. Downstream calculations must
know which interpretation applies.

An exact binary example shows the consequence of retaining alternatives.
In model \(F\), a binary offer \(A\) is Bernoulli with probability one half,
and response \(Y\) equals \(A\) with probability \(0.9\). In model \(R\),
\(Y\) is Bernoulli with probability one half, and \(A\) equals \(Y\) with
probability \(0.9\). Both models produce
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &Y=0&Y=1\\\hline
A=0&9/20&1/20\\
A=1&1/20&9/20
\end{array}.
\]
In \(F\), setting \(A\) from zero to one changes \(E[Y]\) by \(0.8\).
In \(R\), intervening on the equation for \(A\) leaves \(Y\) unchanged.
The two compatible constructions therefore imply the effect candidates
\(\{0,0.8\}\). A directional suggestion favoring \(F\) does not provide
new identifying information unless its underlying premise is independently
justified. These finite calculations are project constructions, not a
calibrated confidence set for a learned graph.

More generally, for a declared graph class \(\mathcal G\), one relevant
downstream object is
\begin{equation}
 \Theta(P,Q,\mathcal G)=\bigcup_{G\in\mathcal G}\Theta_G(P,Q),
 \label{la:graph-union}
\end{equation}
where \(\Theta_G(P,Q)\) contains effects compatible with distribution \(P\),
question \(Q\) and the model restrictions for \(G\). A nonidentified member
can make the union broad. A list of estimated points is not automatically
the whole union, and graph-selection uncertainty cannot be replaced with
ordinary coefficient uncertainty after selecting one member.

Equation~\eqref{la:graph-union} also clarifies what a disagreement review
should resolve. If two experts differ only on an edge that leaves the target
functional unchanged, that disagreement may be immaterial for the current
decision while still mattering for another target. If their graphs imply
different effect signs or feasibility, the conflict is decision-relevant.
The assistant can identify that consequence and prioritize the required
evidence. It should not average expert preferences into an unexplained graph.

\section{Retrieval failure and scientific disagreement}

An evidence assistant can fail to find a passage because the document is
unavailable, parsing failed, the query was poor, the retriever missed it, or
the passage is absent from the inspected document. These cases support
different statements. ``No passage was retrieved'' cannot by itself become
``the authors ignored the assumption,'' and neither statement establishes
that the assumption is false in the population.

The inspected ARGUS paper makes this distinction especially useful. It
audits reported evidence concerning DiD identifying assumptions and does
not claim to adjudicate causal truth. Its synthetic flaw study exhibits a
retrieval/abstention tradeoff, and its small human-label pilot reports an
in-sample calibration change that was not tested on unseen papers. These
observations motivate a banking evidence state that is separate from a
scientific risk judgment.\cite{v12_la_2609_30867}

The proposed record contains the source bytes, the query or retrieval
configuration, inspected anchors and the resulting narrow claim. If evidence
is missing, it records the missing step. If two sources conflict, it records
their populations, dates and definitions before treating the conflict as
substantive. The analyst can then determine whether the sources concern
different regimes or whether a genuine contradiction remains.

This process does not require pretending that every edge has a published
study behind it. Some causal premises depend on institutional facts: which
system sets a rate, when a policy becomes visible, how an audit was selected,
or which identifier establishes ownership. Those facts need an accountable
owner and authentic records. Literature retrieval can help formulate the
questions, but it cannot supply an institution's missing assignment truth.

The proposed interaction starts with a question and variable definitions,
then records diagram alternatives. Each edit changes a declared object:
add or remove a variable, refine a clock, replace a proxy, propose an endpoint,
or accept a restriction. The edit retains its predecessor identity and
reason. A reviewer can therefore see whether an apparent improvement in
fit came from a new assumption, a different target, or an actual correction
of an error.

Formal checks can reject a directed cycle in a DAG, impossible declared
time order or an explicitly forbidden direction. They can flag mediator,
collider or common-ancestor patterns in the supported representation. Such
checks help maintain a coherent declaration but do not cover every graph

\chapter{Variables, diagrams and justified disagreement}
\label{la:diagrams}

The preceding chapter established what definitions and fallible evidence can
contribute. Here those objects enter a reviewable diagram. The argument first
separates graph classes, premises and retrieval outcomes, then develops exact
proxy, collider, clock and disagreement examples. The ontology comparison
connects the diagram to implementable treatment versions and source records.
The final restrictions study follows a premise through both graph and effect
sets, showing why a smaller graph class need not settle the decision.

\section{From vocabulary to measured variables}

A useful causal diagram begins with variables whose meanings can survive
contact with data. A business glossary may contain ``risk,'' ``relationship''
and ``engagement,'' while a dataset contains a risk-score vintage, a set of
linked accounts and an observed click. Those are related concepts, but they
are not interchangeable causal variables. An assistant can propose mappings,
detect inconsistent names and assemble definitions. Each proposed mapping
still needs an operational meaning, a unit and an information clock.

OntoLearner offers relevant modular ideas for ontology loading, typing,
taxonomy and relation-learning tasks. The inspected paper reports
domain-dependent errors and retrieval failures. Its relation-learning
capability is not a guarantee that a relation is causal, or that a concept
has a valid measured proxy in the bank. Ontology alignment should therefore
precede and inform graph construction without being silently promoted into
causal identification. \cite{v12_la_2607_01977}

For example, ``customer owns account'' may describe a legal relation,
``records share an identifier'' an administrative relation, and ``records
have a high linkage score'' a model output. If ownership affects both offer
eligibility and repayment behavior, substituting the linkage score for
ownership leaves a measurement problem. Adding an arrow from the score to
repayment does not resolve it. The diagram should distinguish latent
ownership, observed records, the linkage procedure and sample selection.

Likewise, an ordinal description such as ``high influence'' cannot be used
as an effect size without a scale. An assistant's rating of a proposed edge
may express a preference among textual explanations. It is not automatically
a probability that the edge is present, a posterior over graphs, or a
confidence level. A typed diagram can retain such a rating as explicitly
uncalibrated metadata while refusing to use it as scientific evidence.

\section{What an edge asserts}

An edge proposal should state more than two variable names. The endpoint
marks identify the proposed graphical object. A source and inspected anchor
state what supports the proposal. A scope describes the population, period
and intervention to which that evidence applies. A counterevidence record
states whether contrary evidence was found, absent in the inspected material,
or not successfully searched. A review disposition records acceptance as a
premise, rejection, or unresolved status.

These fields serve different purposes. A source can be authentic but
inapplicable to the current banking action. A study can concern a different
population or a different definition of treatment. A plausible timing argument
can constrain direction without establishing that any causal connection
exists. The assistant should make the supported proposition as narrow as
the evidence warrants and retain the reasons for disagreement.

CausalChat supplies an example of interactive model development: the inspected
paper combines optional CPDAG discovery, model suggestions, graph editing
and structural-equation coefficient updates. Its prompts use ordinal
causal-significance ratings and ask for possible confounders and mediators.
These are useful interaction ideas. The paper's expert feedback also raises
missing citations and uncertainty about the quality of scientific evidence
provided by the model. A coefficient update after adding an edge cannot
establish that the edge itself is true. \cite{v12_la_2410_14146}

The proposed banking workflow retains the interaction but changes the
scientific handoff. An accepted premise is labeled as a premise with a
responsible review, not as a truth certified by the model. A model proposal
alone cannot remove an observationally compatible graph alternative. The
tool responsible for formal identification receives the complete reviewed
graph object and its restrictions, rather than a picture whose uncertainty
has disappeared in editing.

\section{Graph classes and collections of candidate models}

A CPDAG or PAG is a structured representation with its own interpretation.
A list of proposed DAGs is another object. A collection of edges marked
``possible'' is not automatically an enumeration of every combination of
those edges. Confusing these representations can silently exclude models
or include incompatible ones.

The project contract preserves a CPDAG or PAG directly when that is the
appropriate object, including circle endpoints. It also permits explicitly
listed candidate models. An edge marked possible within a candidate describes
the evidence status of that candidate's edge; it does not make all optional
edge combinations an exhaustive graph class. Downstream calculations must
know which interpretation applies.

An exact binary example shows the consequence of retaining alternatives.
In model \(F\), a binary offer \(A\) is Bernoulli with probability one half,
and response \(Y\) equals \(A\) with probability \(0.9\). In model \(R\),
\(Y\) is Bernoulli with probability one half, and \(A\) equals \(Y\) with
probability \(0.9\). Both models produce
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &Y=0&Y=1\\\hline
A=0&9/20&1/20\\
A=1&1/20&9/20
\end{array}.
\]
In \(F\), setting \(A\) from zero to one changes \(E[Y]\) by \(0.8\).
In \(R\), intervening on the equation for \(A\) leaves \(Y\) unchanged.
The two compatible constructions therefore imply the effect candidates

new identifying information unless its underlying premise is independently
justified. These finite calculations are project constructions, not a
calibrated confidence set for a learned graph.

downstream object is
\begin{equation}

\end{equation}
where \(\Theta_G(P,Q)\) contains effects compatible with distribution \(P\),
question \(Q\) and the model restrictions for \(G\). A nonidentified member
can make the union broad. A list of estimated points is not automatically
the whole union, and graph-selection uncertainty cannot be replaced with
ordinary coefficient uncertainty after selecting one member.

should resolve. If two experts differ only on an edge that leaves the target
functional unchanged, that disagreement may be immaterial for the current
decision while still mattering for another target. If their graphs imply
different effect signs or feasibility, the conflict is decision-relevant.

An evidence assistant can fail to find a passage because the document is

different statements. ``No passage was retrieved'' cannot by itself become
``the authors ignored the assumption,'' and neither statement establishes
that the assumption is false in the population.

fit came from a new assumption, a different target, or an actual correction

\section{Equal observed laws can imply different intervention answers}
\label{v13:la-equivalence}

A diagram assistant must recognize when available observations cannot determine
the requested direction or effect. Consider two project-constructed binary
models. Let $U$ be fair Bernoulli and $A=U$. In model one $Y=A$; in model two
$Y=U$. Both observed datasets contain only $(A,Y)=(0,0)$ and $(1,1)$ with equal
probability. Under an intervention setting $A=a$, model one has mean outcome
$a$ while model two has mean outcome $1/2$. Their average effects are one and
zero. Exact enumeration establishes the discrepancy.\cite{v13_project_exact}

Estimating the observed marginal propensity as $1/2$ does not solve the
problem: exchangeability given the available information is precisely what is
missing. A model that recognizes a plausible causal story may prefer one graph,
but that preference is not identification from these data. Expert knowledge,
measurements or experiments could distinguish the worlds; those inputs need
their own evidence and should remain visible in the result.

A continuous version shows why effect sets can be unbounded. Let independent
standard Gaussian variables $U$ and $\varepsilon$ generate
\[
 X=U,\qquad Y=bX-bU+\varepsilon.
\]
The factual law is $X=U,Y=\varepsilon$ for every real $b$. Under
$\operatorname{do}(X=x)$, however, the mean of $Y$ is $bx$. Therefore every
real intervention slope is compatible with the same observed distribution
within this allowed model class. More observations estimate that common law
more accurately; they do not select $b$. A discovery tool or language model
cannot remove this ambiguity without an additional restriction.

This is a useful evaluation case for agentic discovery. A high-quality response
retains the competing models, explains their observational equivalence and
identifies the information that could separate them. An overconfident single
graph should be scored as a substantive error even if its prose is convincing.
A refusal or whole-line effect set can be the scientifically correct output;
its lack of immediate decision usefulness should be reported separately.

\section{Prior knowledge needs a typed evidence record}

The inspected DirectLiNGAM interface distinguishes a directed path, no directed
path and unspecified prior knowledge. The y0 identification dispatcher requires
a supplied graph rather than eliciting its truth. These interfaces make the
translation from narrative evidence to formal restrictions consequential.
An agent saying ``A is likely relevant to Y'' has not supplied a justified
directed-path constraint.\cite{v13_sw_lingam,v13_sw_y0}

For each proposed restriction, a useful record distinguishes a temporal order,
an intervention mechanism, a measured association, a domain assertion and a
formal exclusion. It binds the variables, their measurement/availability clocks,
the source passage, the supporting scope and any disagreement. A source about
one population or intervention need not justify a hard exclusion in another.
The record should preserve which conclusions change if the assertion is removed.

Suppose a manager states that a rate change cannot be caused by next month's
withdrawal. That supports a temporal ordering when the rate decision was fixed
before the withdrawal. It does not rule out an earlier expectation of withdrawal
affecting the rate, or a common market shock affecting both. A diagram assistant
can expose the omitted expectation variable and the common-cause alternative.
It should not convert the temporal statement into unconfoundedness.

An analogous issue arises in network diagrams. MossSpider's selected source
uses a directed influence convention that requires explicit checking, while a
bank may draw arrows from guarantor to beneficiary. A language model can produce
the correct-looking graph but an incorrectly oriented adjacency representation.
A two-node semantic test with known distinct attributes is more informative
than a visual similarity score.\cite{v13_sw_mossspider}

\section{Set-valued reasoning should survive verbal reporting}

If uncertainty concerns several graphs or nuisance parameters, the effect
object may be a union of intervals. A project ratio example illustrates the
boundary. Let a numerator lie in $[1,2]$ and an audit multiplier in
$[-1/2,1/2]$, with the relation $m=r\theta$. Excluding division by zero while
retaining all feasible nonzero multipliers gives
\[
 \Theta=(-\infty,-2]\ \cup\ [2,\infty).
\]
The gap around zero and the unbounded tails are substantive. Replacing this
object by its hull loses the exclusion of zero; replacing it by a finite
interval loses compatible effects. A monetary transformation should be applied
to each component and preserve endpoint inclusion and infinite endpoints.

The agent should describe why the set is disconnected, what assumptions support
it and what information would make it more useful. It should not translate
``wide uncertainty'' into an invented central estimate. When both zero numerator
and zero multiplier remain jointly feasible, the effect can instead be the
whole real line. The distinction depends on the joint region, not just
separate point estimates.

This reasoning also separates model plausibility from sampling coverage. If a
joint confidence region contains the true observable and nuisance parameters,
its effect image contains the true effect on that event. The implication is
elementary; constructing the valid joint region under the bank's actual
dependence and audit law is the difficult statistical work. An agent can
propagate a supplied region faithfully. It cannot infer that its coverage is
valid merely because the downstream set arithmetic passed a test.

\section{Domain knowledge as evidence for a causal graph}
\label{exec22:domain-scope}

A collections manager considering a payment holiday needs to distinguish a
plausible story from an intervention that improves customer outcomes. A language
model may suggest that financial strain affects delinquency, that servicing
changes financial strain, and that earlier delinquency affects the servicing
offer. Each statement needs a population, a time index, a variable definition
and an evidential basis. Joining the three statements without those qualifications
can create a cycle whose meaning is unclear. A retrieval system can help locate
the underlying evidence, but a retrieved sentence does not by itself establish
an invariant structural mechanism. Two recent clinical studies make the promise
and the limitations of this assistance concrete.

\subsection{Graph elicitation and the meaning of completeness}
\label{exec22:domain-elicitation}

Aziz and Brookhart study a hypothetical comparison of statins with no treatment
for preventing cardiovascular disease. They run four prompting strategies on
GPT-4o and a zero-shot strategy on GPT-o1, with three separate conversations per
configuration. Two author reviewers assess consistency, acyclicity, source
accuracy, completeness and prompt adherence. This is a study of fifteen outputs
in one familiar clinical scenario, rather than an estimate of performance over
a population of banking questions. The original was published on 30 October
2025.\cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

Its completeness criterion asks whether the graph contains seven groups of
variables drawn from an ASCVD risk score. This is a useful check for conspicuous
omissions, but it does not validate the graph's arrows or establish that its
adjustment set identifies the statin effect. Predictors can have different causal
roles: a pretreatment common cause, a mediator and a selection variable cannot
be treated interchangeably simply because each predicts the outcome. In a bank,
a strong arrears predictor measured after a servicing offer may be an outcome
of that offer. Including it in a list is different from correctly deciding
whether to adjust for it.

Table 1 and the article's accompanying text report fourteen acyclic graphs and
seven graphs containing six of the seven criteria. The seven-of-fifteen count
does not support the abstract's ``more than half'' wording. Race is absent from
all fifteen outputs. That is a reproducible observation about the study's
criterion; it does not establish a universal requirement to insert a particular
attribute into every causal model. A social attribute's role needs an explicit
account of the processes it represents and the target population. Blindly
adding a variable to improve a checklist score could conceal the same scientific
problem as omitting it.\cite{exec22_domain_aziz,exec22_domain_reference}

The study also separates producing citations from producing reliable evidence.
One-shot outputs supply sources but include nonexistent references and incorrect
titles, dates or author details. Chain-of-thought outputs give explanations
without sources in all three runs. The GPT-o1 zero-shot configuration consistently
supplies references and code, yet one code output needs manual repair. Its third
run is described as supplying nine sources and then assessed using denominators
of six; the original outputs are needed before aggregating that run's citation
accuracy. The source assessments described in the paper use title and abstract
review, which is weaker than checking that primary methods and results support
a particular causal arrow.\cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

One instruction-based output contains arrows in both directions between statin
use and cholesterol. The authors correctly identify the need for temporally
indexed nodes if feedback is intended. The banking counterpart is
\(D_t\to A_t\to D_{t+1}\), where \(D_t\) is delinquency information available
before action \(A_t\). Collapsing \(D_t\) and \(D_{t+1}\) into a single
``delinquency'' node loses the information clock. A graph assistant should request
that missing distinction rather than silently reverse an arrow to satisfy a
syntactic check. The study supports a brainstorming and source-checking role;
it supplies no validation of a bank effect estimator.

\subsection{Retrieval helps under a particular reference and query}
\label{exec22:domain-retrieval}

Lin and colleagues combine language models, retrieval and observational discovery
for chronic low back pain. Their February 2026 medRxiv original is a preprint,
not a peer-reviewed result. They use baseline observations from 1,868 participants
and a fourteen-variable expert reference. Crucially, the authors explicitly state
that this reference contains cycles and is not a DAG. The reference was developed
from clinical expertise and a literature synthesis; it is a declared comparison
target, not observed intervention truth.\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

The three knowledge systems share Mistral 7B-Instruct v0.3. Ordinary retrieval
supplies document chunks selected by vector similarity. Knowledge-graph retrieval
extracts entities and relations, merges entities, forms communities and retrieves
entities, attached relations, community summaries and supporting text. The paper
describes 600-token chunks with 100-token overlap, an 8,000-token retrieval budget,
and a pipeline involving constrained extraction, a graph database and community
clustering. These are descriptions of the authors' system; they do not establish
that its dependencies are pinned, licensed for the proposed distribution or
operationally integrated here.\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

Both retrieval systems use the same source articles that the experts used to
construct the comparison graph. This is an informative test of reconstructing
an aligned body of knowledge. It does not measure performance when the literature
is incomplete, contradictory, selected by a different team, or independent of the
reference adjudicators. The authors discuss this alignment explicitly. Their
argument that the model predates publication of the expert graph also does not
by itself authenticate the model's training corpus or exclude related earlier
content. The appropriate extension is a deliberately held-out reference and
document design, not a declaration that contamination has been ruled out.

For the data component, the paper describes hill climbing with local generalized
linear models, BIC scores and 500 bootstrap samples. A thresholded consensus graph
forms the initial model. The system then combines its edges with the knowledge
system's proposals and asks a further direction question when both directions
are suggested. Plausibility, association, temporality and a direct causal query
are separate prompt conditions. Their relative performance matters as much as
the strongest result.\cite{exec22_domain_lin}

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{p{0.48\linewidth}rr}
\hline
Reported configuration & F1 & Difference \\
\hline
Observational initial model & 0.396 & --- \\
Initial model plus LLM, plausibility & 0.636 & --- \\
Initial model plus ordinary retrieval, plausibility & 0.714 & --- \\
Initial model plus graph retrieval, plausibility & 0.745 & 0.031 over 0.714 \\
Graph retrieval alone after direction resolution & 0.737 & 0.008 below 0.745 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

These are displayed scores against the single expert graph. The improvement
from 0.396 to 0.745 is 0.349, but the extra gain over ordinary retrieval is 0.031,
and the gain from adding observational discovery to the strongest graph-retrieval
configuration is 0.008. None is a paired confidence interval or a measured return
on engineering effort. Before direction resolution, graph retrieval's plausibility
F1 is 0.602, below the LLM-only value of 0.627. After resolution the values are
0.737 and 0.636. In the final combined systems, ordinary retrieval exceeds graph
retrieval for association by 0.060 and for temporality by 0.130. A blanket ranking
of retrieval architectures would conceal these reversals.\cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

The strongest combined configuration still reports FDR 0.360, meaning disagreement
among its predicted directed edges against this reference under the paper's
definition. It is not a certified probability that a proposed bank causal claim
is false. Small differences also deserve care: subtracting the printed 0.396
from 0.636 gives 0.240, whereas Table 5 prints a change of 0.241. Rounding of
unreported underlying values can explain that discrepancy. It supplies a reason
to recover the original edge records, not a reason to invent corrected results.

\subsection{Direct edges, indirect effects and feedback need different objects}
\label{exec22:domain-semantics}

The chronic-pain plausibility and temporality questions explicitly allow a
relationship ``through one or more intermediate variables.'' Their answers
therefore need not describe direct adjacency among the measured variables.
For the chain
\begin{equation}
 A\longrightarrow M\longrightarrow Y,
 \qquad E=\{(A,M),(M,Y)\},
 \label{exec22:domain-chain}
\end{equation}
\(A\) is an ancestor of \(Y\) even though \((A,Y)\notin E\). A positive
indirect-effect answer cannot be inserted as a direct edge without changing the
graph and possibly its conditional independences. Conversely, when a variable
is unmeasured, a projected graph may legitimately have different edge semantics.
The interface must state which object it is constructing. The paper's source
text is sufficient to identify the mismatch that needs checking; it is not
sufficient to reconstruct every edge's intended semantics.\cite{exec22_domain_lin,exec22_domain_reference}

Taking a union of proposed edges also has no universal accuracy guarantee.
Starting from the correct two-edge set in equation~\eqref{exec22:domain-chain},
adding the false edge \(Y\to A\) produces two true positives, one false positive
and no false negatives. Thus
\begin{equation}
 F_1=\frac{2\,\mathrm{TP}}{2\,\mathrm{TP}+\mathrm{FP}+\mathrm{FN}}
     =\frac45<1.
 \label{exec22:domain-f1}
\end{equation}
It also creates a directed three-cycle without any reciprocal pair. Resolving
only two-way pairs would not remove it. This exact example does not assert that
the paper's code necessarily produces such a failure. It shows why the observed
nonnegative changes in its result table cannot be promoted to a theorem that
combining knowledge and data always improves the graph.\cite{exec22_domain_reference}

There is a further distinction in the observational comparison. Moralization
drops arrowheads and connects parents of a common child. For
\(A\to M\leftarrow B\), it adds the \(A\)--\(B\) link even though that link
is absent from the original skeleton. Consequently, the paper's moralized-graph
comparison is not simply a comparison of adjacencies after ignoring direction.
Good agreement on that object cannot identify a unique causal ordering. Similarly,
a cyclic expert reference and a DAG learner require an explicit account of the
representation mismatch before their distance is interpreted as scientific error.

A useful banking representation retains the proposition type, time horizon,
population, supporting span and evidence strength for each proposed relation.
It distinguishes a direct cause from an ancestor, an association, an ontological
relationship and a modeler's assumption. A type hierarchy or a semantic link in
a knowledge graph is not automatically a causal edge. Hard constraints can narrow
the graph search when justified by an information clock or design rule. Uncertain
literature claims should remain revisable evidence; treating them as inviolable
constraints can exclude the true graph. When sources conflict, returning the
alternatives preserves information that forced orientation destroys.

\subsection{Identical records can support opposite investment decisions}

plausible story from an intervention that improves customer outcomes. A language
model may suggest that financial strain affects delinquency, that servicing
changes financial strain, and that earlier delinquency affects the servicing
offer. Each statement needs a population, a time index, a variable definition
and an evidential basis. Joining the three statements without those qualifications
can create a cycle whose meaning is unclear. A retrieval system can help locate
the underlying evidence, but a retrieved sentence does not by itself establish
an invariant structural mechanism. Two recent clinical studies make the promise
and the limitations of this assistance concrete.

for preventing cardiovascular disease. They run four prompting strategies on
GPT-4o and a zero-shot strategy on GPT-o1, with three separate conversations per
configuration. Two author reviewers assess consistency, acyclicity, source
accuracy, completeness and prompt adherence. This is a study of fifteen outputs
in one familiar clinical scenario, rather than an estimate of performance over
a population of banking questions. The original was published on 30 October
2025. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz}

variables drawn from an ASCVD risk score. This is a useful check for conspicuous
omissions, but it does not validate the graph's arrows or establish that its
adjustment set identifies the statin effect. Predictors can have different causal
roles: a pretreatment common cause, a mediator and a selection variable cannot
be treated interchangeably simply because each predicts the outcome. In a bank,
a strong arrears predictor measured after a servicing offer may be an outcome
of that offer. Including it in a list is different from correctly deciding
whether to adjust for it.

Table 1 and the article's accompanying text report fourteen acyclic graphs and
seven graphs containing six of the seven criteria. The seven-of-fifteen count
does not support the abstract's ``more than half'' wording. Race is absent from
all fifteen outputs. That is a reproducible observation about the study's
criterion; it does not establish a universal requirement to insert a particular
attribute into every causal model. A social attribute's role needs an explicit
account of the processes it represents and the target population. Blindly
adding a variable to improve a checklist score could conceal the same scientific
problem as omitting it. \cite{exec22_domain_aziz,exec22_domain_reference}

titles, dates or author details. Chain-of-thought outputs give explanations
without sources in all three runs. The GPT-o1 zero-shot configuration consistently

run is described as supplying nine sources and then assessed using denominators

accuracy. The source assessments described in the paper use title and abstract
review, which is weaker than checking that primary methods and results support
